mainEntity.name: How Long Does a SolusVM HA Failover Take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Detection is bounded by the watchdog and the grace period you configure, then each virtual server boots. Budget the grace period plus a normal cold boot per server, and test it on your own hardware rather than trusting an estimate.

mainEntity.name: Can a Network Outage Trigger a False Failover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not on its own. If the compute resource still holds its storage lock, SolusVM considers it active even when the management node cannot reach it. Evacuation waits on lock expiry, not on reachability.

mainEntity.name: Do Virtual Servers Move Back Automatically After the Node Recovers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. They keep running where HA placed them. Moving them back to the original compute resource is a manual action.

mainEntity.name: How Many Compute Resources Can One Failover Domain Hold?

acceptedAnswer.text: Up to 2,000. Capacity headroom becomes the real limit long before that number does.

@graph.name: How to Set Up a SolusVM High Availability Failover Domain
@graph.description: The prerequisites a SolusVM failover domain needs before HA will evacuate virtual servers off a failed compute resource.

step.name: Enable High Availability protection globally
step.text: HA protection has to be enabled globally before any failover domain configuration takes effect.

step.name: Put at least two compute resources in the domain
step.text: A failover domain needs at least two compute resources. A domain of one has nowhere to evacuate to.

step.name: Standardise the domain on KVM and shared storage
step.text: Every compute resource in the domain must run KVM virtual servers on Shared LVM over iSCSI or NFS. Virtuozzo compute resources are not supported, even when the servers on them are KVM.

step.name: Give the domain its own dedicated storage
step.text: Use one shared storage backend per failover domain. Sharing a single storage backend across two domains is not a supported setup.

step.name: Leave capacity headroom on every node
step.text: Each compute resource needs enough free CPU and memory to run the virtual servers evacuated from a failed peer. Four nodes at 90% utilisation have nowhere to place anything.

step.name: Configure Disaster Recovery alongside it
step.text: If HA cannot place a virtual server and that server has a valid backup, Disaster Recovery recreates and restores it onto healthy compute resources one at a time. Test the restore path before you need it.
